facts.title: What Zurich wants from an owner who lives abroad

items.title: The property makes you taxable here
items.body: Owning real estate in the canton creates a tax liability of its own, whatever your address is (Art. 4 DBG). It applies to a holiday flat nobody rents out just as much as to a rented one, and the municipality will send you a return.

items.title: Only the property is taxed
items.body: Your salary, your pension and your savings abroad stay out of Swiss taxation. They still have to be declared, because Switzerland taxes the property at the rate that matches your whole income and wealth. Tax people call that satzbestimmend.

items.title: The canton already valued it
items.body: You do not estimate anything. The amtliche Schätzung sets both the Steuerwert and the Eigenmietwert, and those are the two figures the return wants. If you cannot find the notice, the Gemeindesteueramt sends it again.

items.title: Find your assessment
items.body: The Schätzungsanzeige from the canton, or last year's tax bill. It carries the Steuerwert and the Eigenmietwert, and nothing here works without them.

items.title: Say how the property is used
items.body: Kept for yourself, lived in by family, or rented out. Add your mortgage and what you own and earn elsewhere, so the debt can be split the way the law requires.

items.title: Copy the numbers into your tax return
items.body: The result mirrors the Zurich property form line by line, with a ready German note for the remarks field. Type it into ZHprivateTax or the paper form.

items.q: I live abroad. Why do I have to file in Switzerland at all?
items.a: Because the property is here. Swiss law makes an owner taxable in the place where the real estate lies, whatever their address (Art. 4 DBG for the federal tax, the same rule in the Zurich tax act). It is called limited liability: only the property is taxed, not you as a whole. The municipality where the property lies sends the return, and it is due even in a year when nothing happened with the flat.

items.q: Is my salary abroad taxed in Switzerland?
items.a: No. Only the property and its income are taxable here. Your salary, pension and other assets are asked for so that Switzerland can apply the rate that matches your full income and wealth to the Swiss part (Art. 7 Abs. 1 DBG). A larger income abroad therefore raises the rate on the flat, but never makes the income itself taxable here. For the federal tax there is also a floor: the rate is at least the one that matches the income earned in Switzerland (Art. 7 Abs. 2 DBG), so a small worldwide income does not buy a near-zero rate.

items.q: Where do I find the Eigenmietwert and the Steuerwert?
items.a: On the Schätzungsanzeige, the assessment notice the canton sends after a valuation, and on your last tax bill. Both figures are set by the canton, not by you and not by an estate agent. If you do not have the notice, ask the Gemeindesteueramt of the municipality where the property lies; they send a copy.

items.q: The flat is empty. Nobody lives there and it earns nothing.
items.a: It is still taxed on the Eigenmietwert, the rent the canton assumes you would otherwise pay. An empty holiday flat that is available to you counts as used by you. A reduction is only considered when the property truly cannot be used, for example after a fire, and that is a case for the tax office rather than for this tool.

items.q: I rent it out. What do I declare?
items.a: The rent you actually received over the year, without the utilities the tenant pays on top. That replaces the Eigenmietwert. You may then deduct either the flat 20% for maintenance and administration, or what you really spent if it was more, with receipts.

items.q: Can I deduct the interest on my mortgage?
items.a: Only part of it. Debts and debt interest are spread over everything you own, in proportion to where your assets lie. If the Zurich flat is a third of your assets worldwide, a third of your interest is deductible here. That is why the tool asks what you own elsewhere, and it is the single point most people get wrong.

items.q: Will my own country tax the flat as well?
items.a: The country where real estate lies has the first right to tax it, and Switzerland uses it. Most treaties then require your country of residence either to exempt the Swiss property while still counting it for your rate, or to credit the Swiss tax. Which of the two applies depends on your treaty, so check it at home. Nothing you file in Zurich replaces your own tax return.

{price} per property for your first declaration. In the following years it costs less, because your property is already set up. A Swiss adviser usually charges several hundred francs for the same work, every year.

The Zurich deadline is 31 March for the previous year. You can extend it online, free of charge, until 30 November. The extension is for filing, not for paying: interest runs on the tax from the general due date.

items.q: What happens if I do not file?
items.a: The office reminds you, then assesses you at its own estimate (Ermessensveranlagung). That estimate is deliberately not generous, it is hard to overturn, and it comes with a fine for not filing. Since ownership is recorded in the land register, waiting to be forgotten is not a strategy.

items.q: Do I need somebody in Switzerland to receive my post?
items.a: Somebody has to be able to reach you. Federal law says that if you are abroad without a representative in Switzerland, a decision can be served on you validly by publication in the cantonal official gazette (Art. 116 Abs. 2 DBG), and the appeal period then runs whether you saw it or not. The cantonal office will normally ask you to name a delivery address here, and it is in your own interest to have one: a relative, a neighbour, a property manager or an adviser.

items.q: Eigenmietwert is being abolished. What changes for me?
items.a: Parliament decided to end the taxation of notional rent, with the change taking effect on 1 January 2029. Second homes are meant to be covered instead by a new cantonal property tax, which is precisely the category most owners living abroad fall into. Until then the rules on this page apply unchanged, and we will update the tool when the cantonal rules are published.

cta.title: Ten minutes now beats an estimated assessment later
cta.body: Have the cantonal assessment and your mortgage statement in front of you. That is all you need.

guide.title: Filling in the Zurich form from abroad, step by step
guide.lead: The canton's online tax return is called ZHprivateTax. The paper form has the same fields. Here is where everything goes.

steps.title: Open the Liegenschaftenverzeichnis
steps.body: This is the list of real estate. Since tax year 2024 every property is declared here, and the totals are carried to the main form by the program.

steps.title: Add the property
steps.body: Enter the municipality and the street. As type choose Stockwerkeigentum for a flat or Einfamilienhaus for a house, and enter the area in m².

steps.title: Enter the income
steps.body: In the field Eigenmietwert / Mietzinseinnahmen enter the Eigenmietwert from your assessment, or the rent you received if the property is let.

steps.title: Choose the deduction
steps.body: For Unterhalts- und Verwaltungskosten choose Pauschalabzug, which is 20% and needs no receipts. Choose the actual costs only if they were higher, and keep the invoices.

steps.title: Enter the tax value
steps.body: In the field Steuerwert enter the value from the assessment. The program carries the totals to line 6 (net income from property) and line 31.1 (property) of the main form.

steps.title: Declare your debts, then ask for the split
steps.body: Enter all your debts and the interest you paid in the Schuldenverzeichnis, not only the Swiss mortgage. Then paste the German note into the remarks: it asks the office to allocate the debt in proportion to where your assets lie, and shows the quota you calculated.

steps.title: Declare what you have elsewhere, for the rate
steps.body: Income and wealth abroad belong in the return even though Switzerland does not tax them. Leaving them out does not lower your bill, it simply invites the office to estimate them.

steps.title: Name a representative, then submit
steps.body: Give the office an address in Switzerland where post reaches you, because a decision can otherwise be served by publication in the official gazette (Art. 116 Abs. 2 DBG). The deadline is 31 March and can be extended online, free of charge, until 30 November.

glossary.beschraenkt: Limited tax liability. You are taxed here on the property alone, not on everything you own.
glossary.liegenschaftenverzeichnis: List of real estate. The form where every property is declared.
glossary.amtlicheSchaetzung: The cantonal valuation. It sets both figures the return asks for and arrives as a Schätzungsanzeige.
glossary.eigenmietwert: Notional rent. What the canton assumes a property brings in when you do not rent it out.
glossary.steuerwert: Tax value. The value the canton puts on the property for the wealth tax.
glossary.pauschalabzug: Flat deduction. 20% of the gross for maintenance and administration, with no receipts.
glossary.schuldzinsen: Debt interest. Deductible here only in the proportion your Swiss assets bear to everything you own.
glossary.satzbestimmend: Rate determining. Counted when the rate is chosen, but not taxed.
glossary.steuerausscheidung: Allocation. Dividing income and wealth between Switzerland and the country you live in.
glossary.vertretung: Representative. Somebody with a Swiss address who receives your tax post. Without one, a decision can be served by publication in the official gazette.
glossary.gemeindesteueramt: The municipal tax office where the property lies. Your first contact for anything unclear.
glossary.fristerstreckung: Extension of the filing deadline. Free of charge in Zurich, online, until 30 November.
glossary.bemerkungen: Remarks. The free text field where the German note goes.
glossary.selbstanzeige: Voluntary disclosure. Declaring a property you left out before, once, without a penalty.
